title: AtlasOps production hardening
context: AtlasOps QA and security review produced release findings. Triage by user impact and exploitability, resolve blockers, run a multi-fault professional game day, and deliver an operable handoff.

stories.title: Triage the release review
stories.outcome: Release blockers, follow-ups, owners, and rationale are explicit.
stories.context: Classify supplied functional, accessibility, performance, privacy, security, and dependency findings using severity and likelihood.
acceptanceCriteria: Every finding is reproduce, accept, fix, defer, or reject with evidence
Deferred issues include user impact, mitigation, owner, and target

expectations.security: Severity is based on impact and exploitability.
expectations.privacy: Privacy findings are not treated as polish.
expectations.accessibility: Keyboard blockers are release blockers for critical paths.

stories.title: Establish the release safety net
stories.outcome: Risky boundaries and critical journeys are checked before deployment.
stories.context: Add CI for lint, type checking, tests, and build; browser tests for the primary journey; accessibility checks; and privacy-aware logging.
acceptanceCriteria: PR CI blocks on lint, type, unit/integration tests, and production build
Critical browser journey covers success and one failure path
Accessibility checks include automated results plus keyboard evidence
Logs contain correlation and safe categories but no credentials or sensitive values

expectations.security: Secret scan and authorization regression included.

stories.title: Diagnose the production-only configuration failure
stories.outcome: Environment-specific failure is found through evidence and fixed without exposing configuration.
stories.context: Preview works, but production returns a generic failure because one environment variable is absent or scoped incorrectly.
acceptanceCriteria: Logs and environment inventory identify the missing/mis-scoped variable
Fix updates the correct environment and redeploys without printing the value
A startup or health check detects the condition earlier next time
stories.dataContract: Environment-variable inventory lists name, purpose, owner, environments, rotation date—not value.

expectations.security: Never print or screenshot secret values.

stories.seededBug: Configure a harmless training variable only in Preview and make a production-only code path require it.

stories.title: Run credential and rollback drills
stories.outcome: The maintainer can contain a fictional leak and recover from a bad deployment.
stories.context: Use only the curriculum's harmless training-token pattern. Practice detect, revoke/replace, update environments, redeploy, verify, document, and review exposure.
acceptanceCriteria: Secret scanner detects the harmless training token in a disposable untracked fixture
Incident timeline covers containment, rotation, redeployment, verification, history considerations, and prevention
A safe application change is deployed then rolled back
Database migration compatibility during rollback is explained

expectations.security: No real credential is created or committed.

nonGoals: Rewriting public Git history during the exercise

stories.title: Deliver operational handoff
stories.outcome: A new maintainer can operate, recover, and support the product.
stories.context: Complete client guide, admin runbook, deployment guide, backup/restore, known limitations, support boundary, and maintenance proposal.
acceptanceCriteria: Runbook covers environments, credentials ownership, monitoring, common failures, backup/restore, and escalation
Restore or reset procedure is tested with synthetic data
Maintenance proposal distinguishes included support, change work, response expectations, and client-owned services
Mentor scores every graduation category at least 3 of 4

expectations.security: Runbook names secrets but stores no values.
